$schema_note: Maps release artifacts to their Nexus Mods targets. To publish, create a GitHub Release tagged '<artifact>-v<version>' (e.g. nczoningdistrictguide-v1.0.0). The release.yml workflow parses the tag, stages contentDir into installDir, zips it as '<fileBaseName>_v<version>.zip' (so 'r6/...' sits at the zip root), attaches the zip to the release, and uploads to Nexus via Nexus-Mods/upload-action (beta.10, v3 upload API). See RELEASING.md.
$paths_note: contentDir = repo folder whose CONTENTS ship. installDir = path inside the zip those contents are placed at (the in-game install path under the Cyberpunk 2077 root). fileBaseName = the download filename stem (version is appended). NC Zoning District Guide is pure redscript - loose .reds files, no WolvenKit packing and no .archive.
$contentdir_note: contentDir is 'r6' and NOT 'r6/scripts/NCZoningDistrictGuide', because the mod ships THREE trees under r6: the scripts, r6/input/nczdg.xml (the Input Loader binding, without which the open key cannot be rebound), and r6/storages/RedscriptConfigFramework/NCZoningDistrictGuide.docs.txt (the in-game documentation page RCF renders in its hub). Narrowing this to the scripts folder silently drops the keybind and the docs page from the download while every test that reads the REPO still passes. Before writing 'the download includes X' anywhere, check this key rather than the repo.
$file_id_note: The Nexus file id is NOT stored here. It lives in a REPOSITORY VARIABLE named NEXUS_FILE_ID_<ARTIFACT> (uppercased, '-' -> '_'), set under Settings > Secrets and variables > Actions > Variables. Two reasons: (1) a file_id DOES NOT EXIST until the mod's first file has been uploaded to Nexus BY HAND, so committing a placeholder commits a lie; (2) it is deployment config, not source. It is a VARIABLE and not a secret because it is an identifier, not a credential -- it authorizes nothing without NEXUSMODS_API_KEY, and masking it would only make a wrong id harder to debug. Get it from the mod page's Files tab > 'API Info' (Nexus labels it 'Group ID'). DO NOT use the file_id from the public v1 API -- that is a different id space and the wrong value looks entirely plausible. The workflow still honours a `file_id` key here as a fallback, but new repos should not set one.
$mod_page_note: Two keys here drive the mod PAGE rather than the file. `update_mod_version` sets the page's headline version to the released file's version: true for a mod's own main artifact, false for any artifact that shares a page with another (an SLM preset would otherwise stamp '1.0.0kp' onto the page). `nexus_mod_id` is the number in the mod page URL; the workflow looks it up at release time to get the internal id the changelog endpoint needs, so a wrong number here costs the changelog and never posts it to the wrong page. The page DESCRIPTION is still manual -- no endpoint in the pipeline touches it.
$pairing_note: THIS MOD RELEASES IN LOCKSTEP WITH NCZoningCore. It hard-requires NCZoningCore 1.0.0+ and @if(ModuleExists(...)) cannot soften that: ModuleExists tests for a MODULE, not a function, so an older Core still compiles the guarded arm and then fails on a missing function - which takes down every redscript mod on the user's machine, not just this one. release-check verifies a mod against ITSELF and cannot see the pairing, so nothing mechanical will catch a half-finished joint version bump. [[CP2077-Mods/wiki/decisions/core-and-guide-release-together-as-1-0-0]]
